To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a recombinant poxvirus vaccine expressing SIV genes and IL-12 genes induced a potent cytotoxic T- lymphocyte response and was able to protect macaques from SIV infection following mucosal challenge with SIV.
a recombinant poxvirus expressing SIV antigens was able to protect macaques from mucosal challenge with SIV, and that the protection was independent of the immune responses elicited.
a recombinant vaccine based on a genetically engineered poxvirus vector, expressing SIV genes, induces a protective immune response against a highly pathogenic strain of SIV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a recombinant poxvirus vaccine that is capable of inducing a strong cytotoxic T- lymphocyte (CTL) immune response against the human immunodeficiency viruses (HIVs).
the development of a recombinant poxvirus vaccine that is effective in the prevention of HIV infection in the rhesusan macaque model, which is considered to be the best model of human AIDS.
the design of recombinant vaccines for HIV-1, the etiological agent of AIDS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NYVAC-SVI is not a perfect vaccine, but it is a vaccine that can be improved and that is worth pursuing.
the NYVAX vaccine, when administered in a prime-boost regimen to a group of rhesus macaques, was able to induce a strong and sustained CTL response against SIV antigens.
the NYVAX-SIV vaccine candidate is effective per se in a model that best mimics the natural route of transmission of human immunodefciency virus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NYVACSIV recombinant is a promising vaccine candidate for the prevention of HIV infection by the mucosa.

the NYVAc-SIV vaccine is a promising vaccine candidate that can be used in conjunction with other vaccine approaches, such as the use of DNA vaccines or other poxvirus vectors, to achieve a broader protection against HIV-1 infection and/or disease.

the NYV AC-SIV recombinants, when administered intramuscularly to macaques, are able to induce a potent CTL response, which, in turn, is able to control viral infection in a fraction of the vaccinees exposed to SIV by the intrarectal route.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a highly attenuated vaccine candidate can induce a protective immune response in macaques against a highly pathogenic SIVmac251 strain, even when the animals are challenged by the intravenous or mucosal routes.
a live attenuated pox virus vaccine candidate can be effective in the animal model best mirroring human AIDS.
the NYVAX-SIV vaccine is effective in preventing infection by SIVmac251 when given intramuscularly and that the vaccine is effective in protecting against mucosal exposure to SIVmac 251.
